canonical_statement: For independent measurable real random variables X_n on a probability space and a fixed c > 0, the real series sum X_n converges almost surely if and only if the large-jump probabilities are summable, the series of expectations of the inclusive truncations converges, and their variances are summable.
domain_and_universes: universe u; Omega : Type u with MeasurableSpace; mu : Measure Omega with IsProbabilityMeasure; X : Nat -> Omega -> Real; c : Real; Prop in universe 0
conclusion: AE omega under mu, the natural-order partial sums of X n omega converge, iff: Summable (mu.real {|X n| > c}); the natural-order partial sums of integral mu (truncate c (X n)) converge; and Summable (variance (truncate c (X n)) mu).
